handbookNote: New Hampshire Real Estate Broker license exam. Part of the 2026-09-03 R26 population-tier broker buildout (population order: UT > NV > IA > AR > KS > MS > ID > NE > WV > HI > NH > MT > RI > DE > SD > ND > AK > VT > WY). Exam vendor: PSI Services LLC, under contract with the New Hampshire Real Estate Commission (NHREC), per the official Candidate Information Bulletin (test-takers.psiexams.com/api/content/bulletin/6529, updated 7/1/2025). Uniform (national) portion: 75 scored items, worth 80 points (some broker items score up to 2 points each, a real documented PSI scoring quirk shared with Hawaii's broker exam -- do not assume 1 item = 1 point), 150 minutes, passing score 56/80 (70%). New Hampshire state portion: 40 items (40 points), 90 minutes, passing score 28/40 (70%). Combo: 115 items, 120 points total, 240 minutes, passing score 84 points (sum of each portion's independent threshold). Passing is a FLAT 70% per section, sections scored/passed INDEPENDENTLY (bulletin: 'you must pass both the National and State portions'); a candidate who fails one portion retakes only that portion. track_registry models this as exam_question_count=115, exam_duration_sec=14400, pass_percent=70, min_correct=81 (round(115*0.70)), following the same literal-flat-percent/section-independent-retake convention as AR/HI. NATIONAL PORTION (75 items, 11 sections) reuses the exact same real PSI national item bank as Iowa/Mississippi/Hawaii (10/5/8/9/19/13/7/5/6/12/6 weighting across Property Ownership/Land Use Controls/Valuation/Financing/Contracts/Agency/Property Disclosures/Property Management/Transfer of Title/Practice of Real Estate/Real Estate Calculations) -- confirmed structurally identical via the official PSI bulletin's content outline. NEW HAMPSHIRE STATE PORTION (40 items, real Broker item counts): Real Estate Commission (3, incl. the Commission's real purpose/duties/powers and its post-2023-reorg disciplinary authority -- RSA 331-A:28/29/30/34/35 were confirmed REPEALED by a 2023 NH occupational-licensing reorganization, 2023 79:336 eff. 9/1/2023, which moved disciplinary/investigation/sanction authority to RSA Chapter 310 (OPLC); real current cites are RSA 310:9 Complaints/Investigations, 310:10 Disciplinary Proceedings, 310:12 Sanctions), Licensure (5, incl. the real $25,000-minimum surety-bond requirement on principal/managing brokers under RSA 331-A:14 -- NH has NO Recovery Fund, this bond is the actual consumer-protection mechanism -- plus 60-hr broker vs 40-hr salesperson education split, 6-compensated-transaction requirement, and RSA 331-A:15/19/12-a also confirmed repealed by the same 2023 reorg, with license-renewal procedure now living in Rea 401 rather than statute), Regulation of Licensee Conduct (11, incl. three genuinely NH-distinctive property disclosure rules -- private water supply Rea 701.03, insulation Rea 701.04, sewage/septic Rea 701.05 -- plus the real RSA 331-A:26 prohibited-conduct list, which has 38 enumerated grounds I-XXXVIII, and RSA 331-A:13 escrow-account rules), Regulation of Agency Conduct (11, New Hampshire's real 5-type statutory agency-relationship menu under RSA 331-A:25-a through 25-f -- seller agent, buyer agent, disclosed dual agent, and two genuinely distinctive types: DESIGNATED agent (25-e, two different licensees at the same firm represent each side, with a real information wall so one designated agent's knowledge is not imputed to the other) and FACILITATOR (25-f, a real non-fiduciary, non-agency role not obligated to keep information confidential)), and New Hampshire Principles and Practice (10, broadest state section spanning RSA 354-A human rights/fair housing -- NH's protected-class list is broader than federal, adding age/marital status/sexual orientation/gender identity/creed --, RSA 477:4-a property disclosure law (now covering radon/arsenic/lead/PFAS/flood per a 2025 amendment, not just radon/lead as the name might suggest), RSA 356-B Condominium Act, RSA 672/674 planning and zoning (incl. the real 5-part RSA 674:33 ZBA variance test), RSA 482-A wetlands, RSA 78-B Real Estate Transfer Tax (corrected from the bulletin outline's stale '78-A' cite, which is actually NH's Meals & Rooms tax -- real rate is $0.75/$100 charged to each of buyer and seller, $20 minimum), RSA 205-A manufactured housing, RSA 540-A landlord-tenant (security deposit cap = greater of one month's rent or $100), RSA 477/478 recordation (NH is a race-notice state per RSA 477:3-a), and RSA 561 intestate succession). Governing law: RSA Chapter 331-A (New Hampshire Real Estate Practice Act) plus the NH Code of Administrative Rules 'Rea' chapters (Rea 100-700), with disciplinary authority now under RSA Chapter 310 per the 2023 reorg. This bank was drafted across 5 new state-topic drafting passes (the 11 national files were reused from ia_re_broker_questions, not redrafted); every drafting agent was pre-warned to independently re-verify the bulletin's own RSA citations rather than trust them, and multiple agents caught real citation drift from NH's 2023 licensing-law reorganization that the PSI bulletin (updated as recently as 7/1/2025) had not caught up to. Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_broker_answers.js.
